'''Anthony Roy West''' [[Fellow of the Royal Society of Edinburgh|FRSE]], [[Fellow of the Royal Society of Chemistry|FRSC]], [[Fellow of the Institute of Physics|FInstP]], [[Fellow of the Institute of Materials, Minerals and Mining|FIMMM]] (born 21 January 1947) is a British [[chemist]] and materials scientist, and Professor of Electroceramics and Solid State Chemistry at the [[University of Sheffield]].<ref name="uosweb">[https://www.sheffield.ac.uk/materials/staff/arwest01 University of Sheffield website]</ref>

==Education==
West was educated at [[The Harvey Grammar School]] and [[University College Swansea]], where he gained a Bachelor of Science in chemistry in 1968.  He then moved to the [[University of Aberdeen]] where he completed a PhD in 1971 under the supervision of [[Fredrik P. Glasser]].<ref name="uosweb" />

He was appointed lecturer at the [[University of Aberdeen]] in 1971 and gained his [[Doctor of Science]] (DSc) from the university in 1984.  He became professor in chemistry in 1989. He then moved to the [[University of Sheffield]] in 1999 to become Head of the Department of Engineering Materials.

==Research==
West's research has covered the synthesis of new [[oxide]] materials, [[crystal structure]] determination and structure-property relations with particular focus on ionic, electronic and mixed ionic-electronic conduction.  This includes lithium ion conductors, oxygen ion conductor and [[Superconductivity|superconductors]]. His research on these new materials has covered a broad range of conducting materials, including {{chem2|Li3VO4}}-{{chem2|Li4(Si,Ge)O4}} solid solutions with high lithium ion conductivity at room temperature,<ref name="jssc1">{{Cite journal |doi = 10.1016/0022-4596(84)90114-2| title = Li+ Ion Conductivity in the System Li<sub>4</sub>SiO<sub>4</sub> - Li<sub>3</sub>VO<sub>4</sub>|journal = Journal of Solid State Chemistry| volume = 53| issue = 3| pages = 369| year = 1984| last1 = Khorassani | first1 = A. | last2 = West | first2 = A. R. }}</ref> the {{chem2|Ca12Al14O33}} oxide ion conductor<ref>{{Cite journal |doi = 10.1038/332525a0| title = High Oxide Ion Conductivity in Ca<sub>12</sub>Al<sub>14</sub>O<sub>33</sub>|journal = Nature| volume = 332| issue = 6164| pages = 525| year = 1988| last1 = Lacerda | first1 = M. | last2 = Irvine | first2 = J.T.S. |last3 = Glasser | first3 = F.P. |last4 = West | first4 = A. R. | bibcode = 1988Natur.332..525L| s2cid = 4348010}}</ref> and much research on [[barium titanate]], such as that on the La-doped {{chem|BaTiO3}} high-[[permittivity]] [[dielectric]].<ref>{{Cite journal |doi = 10.1063/1.371698| title = Electrical and structural characteristics of lanthanum-doped barium titanate ceramics|journal = Journal of Applied Physics| volume = 86| issue = 11| pages = 6355| year = 1999| last1 = Morrison | first1 = F.D. | last2 = Sinclair | first2 = D.C. |last3 = West | first3 = A. R. | bibcode = 1999JAP....86.6355M}}</ref> He discovered the first 5-volt cathode material for lithium battery applications, {{chem2|Li2CoMn3O8}}.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Kawai |first1=H. |last2=Nagata |first2=M. |last3=Tukamoto |first3=H |last4=West |first4=A. R. |title=A novel cathode Li<sub>2</sub>CoMn<sub>3</sub>O<sub>8</sub> for lithium ion batteries operating over 5 volts |journal=Journal of Materials Chemistry |year=1998 |volume=8 |issue=4 |page=837 |doi=10.1039/a800604k}}</ref>

One of his specialties has been development of the electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (see [[dielectric spectroscopy]]) technique for materials characterisation and electrical property measurements.<ref name="malcy1">{{cite journal |last1=Hodge |first1=I. M. |last2=Ingram |first2=M. D. |last3=West |first3=A. R. |title=New Method for Analyzing AC Behaviour of Polycrystalline Solid Electrolytes |journal=Journal of Electroanalytical Chemistry |year=1975 |volume=58 |issue=2 |page=429 |doi=10.1016/0368-1874(75)85015-5}}</ref><ref name="malcy2">{{cite journal |last1=Hodge |first1=I. M. |last2=Ingram |first2=M. D. |last3=West |first3=A. R. |title=Impedance and Modulus Spectroscopy of Polycrystalline Solid Electrolytes |journal=Journal of Electroanalytical Chemistry |year=1976 |volume=74 |issue=2 |page=125 |doi=10.1016/S0022-0728(76)80229-X}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Irvine |first1=J. T. S. |last2=Sinclair |first2=D. C. |last3=West |first3=A. R. |title=Electroceramics: Characterization by Impedance Spectroscopy |journal=Advanced Materials |year=1990 |volume=2 |issue=3 |page=132 |doi=10.1002/adma.19900020304|bibcode=1990AdM.....2..132I }}</ref> He developed the impedance and modulus spectroscopy technique of data analysis with his colleague at Aberdeen, Malcolm Ingram<ref name="malcy1" /><ref name="malcy2" /> and the Almond-West method for ac conductivity data analysis.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Almond |first1=D. P. |last2=Duncan |first2=G. K. |last3=West |first3=A. ==Promotion of solid state and materials chemistry==
West's book ''Solid State Chemistry and its applications''<ref>[https://www.wiley.com/en-gb/Solid+State+Chemistry+and+Its+Applications-p-9780471908746 Publisher's website – Wiley]</ref> and its condensed version "Basic Solid State Chemistry"<ref name="Publisher's website - Wiley">[https://www.wiley.com/en-gb/Solid+State+Chemistry+and+its+Applications%2C+2nd+Edition%2C+Student+Edition-p-9781119942948 Publisher's website – Wiley]</ref> are well-regarded texts in the field.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Dollase |first1=W. A. |title=Review of Solid State Chemistry and its Applications |journal=Acta Crystallographica |year=1985 |volume=B41 |page=454 |doi=10.1107/S0108768185002476|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Parkin |first1=Ivan P |title=Review: Basic Solid State Chemistry |journal=Applied Organometallic Chemistry |year=2000 |volume=14 |page=227 |doi=10.1002/(SICI)1099-0739(200004)14:4<227::AID-AOC949>3.0.CO;2-F}}</ref> An updated version of the former as a student edition was published in 2014.<ref name="Publisher's website - Wiley"/>

West was the founder of the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]]'s ''[[Journal of Materials Chemistry]]'' in 1991<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Editorial |title=250 Good Reasons to read Journal of Materials Chemistry |journal=Journal of Materials Chemistry |year=2006 |volume=16 |issue=28 |page=2865 |doi=10.1039/B608323B}}</ref> and of the "Materials Chemistry" conference series in the UK, organising the first in Aberdeen in 1991.<ref name="JBGmedal"/>

==Awards and honours==
West was awarded the [[John B. Goodenough Award]] of the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]] in 2013 for "his outstanding contributions to our understanding of structure-composition-property relationships in oxide-based materials, and their application in solid state devices, and for his preeminent role in promoting materials chemistry."<ref name="JBGmedal">[https://www.rsc.org/ScienceAndTechnology/Awards/JohnBGoodenoughAward/2013-winner-Goodenough.asp RSC citation for Award, 2013]</ref>

West is a [[Fellow of the Royal Society of Chemistry]], [[Fellow of the Institute of Physics]], [[Fellow of the Institute of Materials, Minerals and Mining]] and Fellow of the [[Royal Society of Edinburgh]].

Awards:
*2013 John B. Goodenough Award in Materials Chemistry, Royal Society of Chemistry
*2009 Griffiths Medal and Prize, Institute of Materials, Minerals and Mining	
*2008 Epsilon de Oro Award, Spanish Society of Ceramics and Glass	
*2007 Chemical Record Lectureship, Chemical Societies of Japan	
*2008/09 Catedra de Excelencia, Universidad Carlos III, Leganés, Spain
*1996 Industrial Award in Solid State Chemistry, RSC
*1988/89 Research Support Fellowship, Royal Society of Edinburgh
*Honorary member of Materials Research Society of India
